Here are several effective tips to help improve your phone's battery life, covering settings adjustments, daily habits, and battery health maintenance:

---

### **1. Display & Screen Settings (Biggest Battery Drain)**
* **Lower screen brightness:** Set brightness to auto-adjust, or manually keep it at a comfortable, lower level.
* **Shorten screen timeout:** Set your display to lock/turn off after 30 seconds or 1 minute of inactivity.
* **Switch to Dark Mode:** If your phone has an OLED/AMOLED screen, using Dark Mode significantly reduces power consumption because black pixels are turned completely off.
* **Lower the refresh rate:** If your phone features a 120Hz display, dropping it to standard 60Hz can noticeably extend battery life.

---

### **2. Manage Apps & Background Activity**
* **Check battery usage:** Go to **Settings > Battery** to identify which specific apps are draining the most power.
* **Disable Background App Refresh:** Prevent apps from refreshing content when you aren’t actively using them (**Settings > General > Background App Refresh** on iPhone, or **Settings > Apps > Special app access > Background usage limits** on Android).
* **Limit push notifications:** Turn off notifications for non-essential apps (social media, games, shopping apps) so your screen doesn’t constantly wake up.
* **Update or delete problem apps:** Keep your apps and OS updated, as updates often include bug and power efficiency fixes. Uninstall apps you rarely use.

---

### **3. Connectivity & Location Services**
* **Manage Location Services (GPS):** Set app location permissions to "While Using the App" rather than "Always," and revoke access from apps that don't need it.
* **Turn off unused radios:** If you're not using Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, or Personal Hotspot, turn them off. 
* **Use Wi-Fi over Cellular:** Whenever available, Wi-Fi uses considerably less power than mobile data.
* **Enable Airplane Mode in low-signal areas:** When you have 1 bar or no service, your phone boosts transmission power to search for a signal, draining battery rapidly.

---

### **4. System Modes & Features**
* **Use Low Power Mode / Battery Saver:** Turn this on when your battery drops below 30–40% (or keep it on during long days away from an outlet). It automatically pauses syncs, reduces performance slightly, and minimizes background tasks.
* **Turn off "Hey Siri" or "Hey Google":** Disabling always-listening voice assistants stops your microphone and processor from continuously monitoring ambient sound.
* **Disable unnecessary vibrations/haptics:** The vibration motor uses more power than ringtones or silent notifications.

---

### **5. Battery Health & Charging Habits**
* **Avoid extreme temperatures:** Heat is the #1 enemy of lithium-ion batteries. Avoid leaving your phone in direct sunlight or in a hot car, and take bulky cases off if the phone gets warm while fast-charging.
* **Check Battery Health:**
  * **iPhone:** Go to **Settings > Battery > Battery Health & Charging**. If Maximum Capacity is below 80%, the battery may need replacement.
  * **Android:** Check **Settings > Battery**, or use manufacturer diagnostics (e.g., Samsung Members) to view battery health status.
* **Keep a portable power bank handy:** If your battery continues to drain quickly throughout the day or during long commutes, carrying a compact 5,000–10,000mAh portable charger is a great backup solution.
